transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hello doctor, thank you for seeing me. I keep forgetting everyday things like appointments and errands, and it’s starting to really mess up taking care of my wife since her stroke, as well as my commitments to the neighborhood garden project. I just feel so overwhelmed trying to keep track of everything lately.

Have you been feeling down or lost interest in things most days recently, or is the main problem your memory getting worse even when your mood feels okay? Did these memory problems start after a major stress like your wife’s stroke, or have they been gradually getting worse over time?

My mood is actually pretty good and I still love my gardening and storytelling, but I just feel incredibly scattered and overwhelmed. These memory and focus issues aren't really new—I've had these tendencies my whole life, even back in primary school—but they only became a major problem after my wife's stroke because of the sudden mountain of appointments and paperwork I have to manage now.

Before your wife’s stroke, did these focus and forgetfulness problems cause trouble in other parts of your life too, like school, work, or home? Or do they mainly become a problem only when you’re under major stress?

Yes, they've always been there; even in primary school, my teachers complained that I couldn't sit still and left my worksheets half-finished. Throughout my adult life and retirement, my days were very loosely structured, so I could easily jump between hobbies without it causing major trouble. It's only now, with the strict demands of managing my wife's care, that these lifelong habits have become a real disaster.

Do these attention and restlessness problems still affect you in more than one setting now—for example at home, during social activities, or when handling finances and paperwork—or only when managing your wife’s care?

Yes, they definitely affect me in multiple areas, not just with my wife's care. At home, I'm constantly messing up our bills and insurance paperwork, and I've had to back out of my roles in the garden and storytelling projects because people feel they can't rely on me to follow through anymore.

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: Lifelong pattern of inattention and hyperactivity/restlessness beginning in primary school, currently causing clinically significant impairment across multiple settings. Symptoms are not better explained by depression, as mood and interest are preserved, and recent caregiver stress appears to have exacerbated pre-existing ADHD traits rather than caused them.
